name: MCP health plugin
summary: watches every live session's mcp servers and puts a yellow ! on a row when one is down; a catalog plugin you install from warez, off until you approve it, with an allow or block list of servers and optional notifications.
description: The MCP server monitor is a catalog plugin (carnivore/mcphealth, sandboxed): it is no longer built into the app, so install it from warez and approve what it asks for. An install that had the built-in copy on keeps its settings, stays off until you approve the new sheet, and gets one alert pointing at warez. Until installed and on: with it off nothing is measured, no server is probed, no client log is read and no row shows the yellow !. Turned on it works as before: for every live Claude Code and Codex session it reads the configured servers, the session's own MCP client log, the stdio processes and a 60 second reachability probe, and names each down server with its reason in the row's tooltip. Its settings choose which servers may raise the !: all of them, only the ones you list, or all but the ones you list. A server left out is still measured but never shows on the row and never notifies. With notifications on, a server that may warn sends one notification when it goes down in a session and one when it comes back, never repeated while it stays down and none in the first minute after Carnivore starts.
where: Menu tab, warez, the mcp health plugin (carnivore/mcphealth); once installed, the plugins page shows its switch and its settings (link: #plugins/mcphealth/settings).
The yellow ! on a session row's menu button and its tooltip, while the plugin is on.
how_to: Open warez from the menu tab, install mcp health, then open the plugins page and press its switch; it asks to read which mcp servers your sessions have and to raise a notice.
In its side pane pick which servers may raise the !: all servers, only the listed servers, or all but the listed servers, and type the server names separated by commas.
Tick send notifications to get one notification when a server goes down in a session and one when it comes back; mute the type mcp server down or back in the notification settings.
examples: A remote server you know is often offline keeps lighting the !; you put it on the block list and the row stays quiet while every other server still warns.
You only care about the carnivore server: you choose only the listed servers and list carnivore.
You turn notifications on and your phone hears once when the memory server drops in a session, and once when it is back.
media_exempt: background measurement plus settings fields drawn by the generic plugin side pane; the row's yellow ! is unchanged from the existing badge
